text: Five centimetres of animal. A house up to a metre wide.
And it builds that house itself — out of mucus.
Two filters, one inside the other — and the inner one is fine enough to trap tiny particles.
When the filters clog, it simply moves out — and builds a new house.
The old one sinks. And not slowly: up to eight hundred metres in a single day.
Scientists call them sinkers. They carry carbon from the surface down into the deep sea.
But scientists found those houses carry something else down with them, too.
What it is — and every other type of deep-sea creature — is linked right here.
